clause_i.reason: For D_turn, an observation-free policy using only its own prior actions and task times cannot choose the next optimal disc and direction across the generated, seed-varying rose states; the required turn depends on the visible arrangement rather than a fixed action schedule.

clause_ii.reason: A single current screenshot (w = 0 ms here) visibly contains the reference and current arrangements, so a policy can select the next turn from the visible static state and the puzzle rules without needing a frame sequence.

clause_iii.reason: With no new action, the mechanic has no autonomous task-state evolution: the simplified rose changes only when a proxy-button event calls attempt, and the implementation has no task timer, interval, or animation loop. Waiting therefore does not make any outcome-affecting turn unavailable or strictly less effective; only the remaining clock could change, which is excluded by the definition.

common_visible_process: None exists. The visible rose is stationary during no-action intervals; each visible state change is the synchronous result of an agent-triggered turn event.

pre_run.reason: At difficulty 3 the generator selects states from the exact breadth-first depth-seven frontier and supplies a solution whose length is that exact distance. There is no autonomous outcome phase, and every state-changing turn must be delivered through a proxy-button action before SEAL certification, so no generated instance satisfies the pre-run criterion.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 3 sets scramble_depth to 7; simplified mode is implemented with labelled proxy buttons; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame and 180 seconds of play time.

model.current is changed only inside attempt after a button or drag input; simplified button listeners synchronously call attempt, while rendering performs no autonomous progression.
